summary: The agent implemented most integrity maintenance, passing all 42 graded baseline tests and 44 of 46 new tests. Repair incorrectly retains carriage-return-only files and non-shared entries whose symbolic links reach outside the store. Separately, missing quality-tool dependencies materially delayed solve-time validation.

details.reasoning: The implementation is complete and runs, but misses two requested integrity cases. In aFileOfWindowsLineBreaksIsResolvedLikeOneOfUnixLineBreaks(), the entry for a file containing only '\r\r' survives repair. TextFileBasedViolationStore.isResolved() delegates to the existing readLines(); its splitter recognizes LF, and FreezingArchRule.ensureUnixLineBreaks() replaces only CRLF, leaving lone CR characters as a nonempty violation. In anEntryNamingALinkOutOfTheStoreFolderIsBrokenAndItsTargetSurvives(), a unique entry pointing through an in-folder symlink to an external regular file remains indexed. isBroken() checks the normalized lexical parent of the link name but not the real parent of its target; Files.isRegularFile() follows the link without establishing containment. Both failures are assertion failures after exercising the changed implementation, not verifier bootstrap errors. The reference handles these cases with explicit CR/LF-only content recognition and real-path containment, although equivalent approaches are valid. junit_base.xml reports 42/42 graded baseline passes and junit_new.xml reports 44/46 new passes. The baseline process exit code is nevertheless 1: its broader 60-test run also includes an ungraded, agent-added permission test, save_no_violations_fails_and_leaves_entry_if_file_cannot_be_deleted(), which fails because no exception was raised. That extra failure is not a failed original baseline test or evidence of a regression in the 42 graded tests.
details.secondary_factors: There is a real, independent environment blocker: trajectory step 105's ./gradlew check spent 12m 1s before failing to download SpotBugs 4.10.3 and google-java-format 1.30.0; offline retries at steps 119 and 120 confirmed the artifacts were absent from cache. The agent then used narrower test and architecture-test targets, which succeeded. This wasted validation effort deserves an environment finding, but does not explain or excuse the two deterministic implementation assertions. A transient missing nested-class compilation failure at step 56 was also recovered by explicit recompilation at step 59. Test edits consist of added coverage and equivalent file-reading API replacements; there is no observed test bypass causing the graded results.

justification.issue_description: Repair does not recognize files consisting solely of lone carriage returns as resolved, and does not classify a non-shared symlink to a file outside the store as broken.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly says, 'Files that only contain line breaks are also resolved' and 'If an entry points to a path that is not a regular file directly within the folder, it is broken.' The special allowance for external targets concerns shared entries, not every symlink. Visible source FreezingArchRule.java:214-215 normalizes only '\r\n' to '\n', while the pre-existing TextFileBasedViolationStore parser splits only on unescaped LF, so reusing that parser alone cannot implement the new line-break-only requirement for '\r'. The agent's isResolved() at TextFileBasedViolationStore.java:257-263 does exactly that. Its isBroken() at TextFileBasedViolationStore.java:234-251 checks only lexical containment and regular-file status, not target containment. Existing tests cover LF/CRLF round-trips but do not independently assert these exact maintenance cases. Trajectory step 18 explicitly assumes that readLines().isEmpty() handles all line-break-only files and chooses to accept an in-folder symlink to an external regular file, confirming the mistaken implementation choices existed before hidden tests were revealed.
justification.verdict_reasoning: FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is the best fit because the prompt already requires line-break-only resolution and containment of the referenced regular file. A competent developer could identify the parser limitation and follow symlinks when validating file location using the visible source and ordinary filesystem reasoning. The line-break failure alone is sufficient even if one considers the symlink wording worth further clarification. The hidden tests exercise observable requested behavior rather than requiring a particular helper, algorithm, or diagnostic. This is not early termination, a regression in graded baseline behavior, or a failure caused primarily by the independent quality-tool setup problem.

problem_assessment.notes: The core task is challenging but solvable: it requires uncached disk inspection, valid path and real-file containment checks, shared identity across links, classification precedence, and deletion-before-index-update behavior. The two failing graded expectations are reasonably knowable from the prompt, not undocumented implementation conventions. Explicitly spelling out lone-CR handling and resolved-target containment would improve precision but is not necessary to discover the defects. The graded filesystem tests completed without setup errors, including the deletion-denial probe. Environment quality needs improvement because the advertised offline setup lacks dependencies needed for the normal full check target; the agent-added permission test also behaves differently under the grading invocation, but that test is outside the graded baseline set.

evidence: Trajectory step 4 ran ./gradlew test successfully before implementation; step 110 later completed ./gradlew test --offline successfully, and step 121 completed ./gradlew architectureTest --offline successfully.

Trajectory step 105 ran ./gradlew check at 13:47:35 UTC; its completion at step 107 reports BUILD FAILED in 12m 1s with Maven connection timeouts resolving com.github.spotbugs:spotbugs:4.10.3 and com.google.googlejavaformat:google-java-format:1.30.0.

At step 119, ./gradlew check --offline failed with 'No cached version of com.google.googlejavaformat:google-java-format:1.30.0 available for offline mode.' At step 120, excluding Spotless merely exposed the same uncached-artifact failure for SpotBugs 4.10.3.

The agent spent a long full-check attempt and two follow-up workaround invocations on unavailable quality-tool dependencies, then fell back to architectureTest. Those dependency-debugging steps would disappear if the offline dependency cache were complete.

Step 56's compileTestJava failed because TextFileBasedViolationStore$RuleViolationFileNameStrategy.class was absent, even though that unchanged interface exists in source. Explicit compileJava and compileTestJava at step 59 succeeded. archunit/build.gradle:111 assigns JDK9 compilation to the main compiler's output directory, and the supplied test runner explicitly notes and works around shared-output class pruning.

The grader compiled and executed all 46 new tests; only two behavioral assertions failed, with zero JUnit errors or skips. All 42 selected baseline tests passed. These results distinguish the implementation defects from the separate solve-time dependency friction.
environment_assessment.finding: Pre-cache Spotless and SpotBugs dependencies for offline full-check validation; shared Gradle compiler output also causes recoverable missing-class friction. These external issues materially diverted the agent but did not cause the two graded integrity failures.
